unresolvedReferences.description: Liu Shao's death in Sui service is undated; c. 610 is a placeholder inference.
The late-Daye events leading to the Taiyuan rising are dated to 617 by inference.
Han Gaozu and King Tang are BCE allusions left unresolved; Wei Taizu (Cao Cao) dated c. 200 by inference.
The defeat by Xue Ju and campaign against Xue Rengao are dated 618 by inference.
Liu Wenjing's execution is dated 619 by inference (born c. 568 from age 52).
Pei Ji's Left Personal Guard posting is only placed in the Kaihuang era (581–600); c. 590 is a placeholder.
Wei Yunqi's accusation is undated; c. 620 inferred.
Pei Ji's exile to Jing Prefecture and death (age 60) are dated c. 630 by inference.
Pei Lüshi's inheritance and marriage to Princess Linhai are dated c. 630 by inference; Chengxian's death under Empress Wu c. 690.
Liu Bang, Xiao He and Cao Shen are BCE allusions left unresolved.
The monk Fayi (法雅) was not offered as a candidate and was not extracted.
The Turkic raid on Mayi is dated c. 622 by inference.
Jiang Yuan's Northern Zhou service is undated; c. 575 is a placeholder.
Jiang Xie's career is undated; c. 650 is a placeholder.
Tuoba Chici's submission is dated c. 635 by inference.
Zhang Jingzang's teaching of Liu Sili is dated c. 670 by inference.
Gongsun Wuda's campaigns against the Turks are dated c. 630 by inference.
Pang Tongshan's office is undated; c. 660 is a placeholder.
Li Che's Sui offices are undated; c. 600 is a placeholder.
Wang Gui's conviction over Wang Pi is dated c. 604 by inference.
Li Mengchang's and Yuan Zhongwen's final offices are undated; c. 626 is a placeholder.
Wei Qing is a BCE allusion left unresolved.
Qin Xingshi's final office is undated; c. 626 is a placeholder.
Xiao He and Cao Shen are BCE allusions left unresolved; Pei Ji's dismissal dated c. 629 by inference.
